correctness.rationale: For every nonnegative integer target order k, chain rule under the smooth double Fourier sphere parametrization and the exact two-dimensional polar Jacobian reduce the torus H^k estimate to finitely many inverse-radius weighted L² norms of derivatives. Frank--Seiringer fractional Hardy Theorem 1.1 with N=p=2 and fractional order 1/2 bounds these from source H^{k+1/2}. Standard Hilbert Sobolev interpolation gives all real t≥0. The smooth north-pole annulus family has source H^s uniformly bounded yet target torus H^t growing at least as epsilon^{s-t-1/2}; its exact one-dimensional Fourier coefficients verify the sharpness for every s<t+1/2. The proof does not infer an infinite result from numerical quadrature.

value.rationale: The 2021 DFS paper highlights a failure of H¹ preservation, creating a natural unresolved question of what source regularity restores torus control. The sharp necessary-and-sufficient critical loss of precisely half a Sobolev derivative is a structural answer for all target orders, not a routine finite calculation; it also provides a concrete s>3/2 criterion for absolute DFS Fourier convergence and rigorously identifies the unavoidable pole concentration mechanism.
